test_title: PYST 26: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - Mathematics (Held On: 20 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: Two pipes can fill a cistern, individually, in 70 min and 30 min, respectively. There is a pipe located at the bottom of the cistern to empty it. If all the three pipes are opened simultaneously, then the empty cistern gets filled in 28 min. How long will the pipe at the bottom of the tank take to empty the completely filled cistern if no other pipe is then open?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Capacity = LCM(70, 30, 28) = 420 units.

Efficiency of Pipe 1 = 420 ÷ 70 = +6, Efficiency of Pipe 2 = 420 ÷ 30 = +14.

Net combined efficiency (filling) = 420 ÷ 28 = +15.

Efficiency of Emptying Pipe = 15 − (6 + 14) = −5 units/min.

Time to empty completely = Total Capacity ÷ Emptying rate = 420 ÷ 5 = 84 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 84 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by the first pipe (A) to fill = 70 min

Time taken by the second pipe (B) to fill = 30 min

Time taken when all pipes (A, B, and emptying pipe C) are open = 28 min

**Method Used:**

Total Capacity is taken as the LCM of the given times. Efficiency = Total Capacity ÷ Time.

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time (min)**
 **Total Capacity**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 First Pipe (A)
 70
 420
 6
 
 

 Second Pipe (B)
 30
 14
 
 

 All Pipes (A + B − C)
 28
 15
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the efficiency of the emptying pipe C be EC units/min.

⇒ Total efficiency when all pipes are open = Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B − EC

⇒ 15 = 6 + 14 − EC

⇒ 15 = 20 − EC

⇒ EC = 5 units/min.

⇒ Time taken by pipe C to empty the completely filled cistern = Total Capacity ÷ Efficiency of C

⇒ Time taken = 420 ÷ 5 = 84 min.

**∴ The correct answer is 84 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Positive and Negative Work

In pipes and cisterns, filling pipes do positive work (+ efficiency) while emptying pipes or leaks do negative work (− efficiency).

Net Filling Rate

When both filling and emptying pipes are open, Net Efficiency = Sum of filling rates − Sum of emptying rates.

Time Taken to Fill/Empty

Total time taken to fill or empty a tank is simply calculated as: Time = Total Capacity (LCM) ÷ Net Efficiency.
